title: Decentralising LLM Alignment: A Case for Context, Pluralism, and Participation

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical evaluation of how current alignment methods (such as RLHF) disproportionately reflect the normative preferences of Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) societies, causing 'mode collapse' and suppressing pluralistic values.

Conceptual analysis utilizing a fictional Voter Advice Application (VAA) case study to evaluate how centrally aligned LLMs might control political information, limit public debate, and potentially exacerbate voter polarization.

Theoretical analysis using a fictional LLM-powered Non-Playable Character (NPC) case study to evaluate the risk of stereotypical depictions, cultural erasure, and representational harms against marginalized and indigenous communities.
